messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager triggered: High outbound QPS from org 'orchid-labs' (org_id: org_0x9a). 95th latency on gpu-cluster-2 spiked to 1.6s, error rate 5.2% (baseline 0.3%). Alert rule: inference.latency.p95 > 1.0s for 2m. Dashboard: https://playback/redwood/d/infra/latency?org=org_0x9a
sara-oncall: oncall here. grabbing logs and tracing. tagging eng/SRE.
sara-oncall: short summary: orchid-labs ramped traffic this morning, probably a loadtest or customer rollout. Autoscaler didn't keep up. We need quick mitigation to protect other customers and reduce error rate.
ryan-sre: I'm at my laptop. can we apply a per-org emergency rate limit or isolate their traffic to dedicated pool? which is faster?
mina-eng: isolating to dedicated pool requires deploy + warmup, slower. emergency per-org rate limit via control plane is immediate. I can run the admin hotpatch.
sara-oncall: leo-support, can you check if CS/AM had a scheduled rollout or notified us? julie-cs loop in please.
leo-support: pinged AM via DM, no reply yet. I left a note to their oncall slack.
julie-cs: got forwarded msg from customer: "we're running smoke for 2.0 launch" — they didn't indicate traffic shape. sending them a temp advisory.
mina-eng: proposed mitigation options:
- Option A: apply emergency throttle (soft limit) for org_0x9a: 120 rpm (tokens) across generation endpoints.
- Option B: disable heavy endpoints (batch-embeddings) for that org.
- Option C: route their traffic to lower-priority pool (if burst capacity available).
sara-oncall: we need to protect p95 for other tenants. prefer Option A first (throttle) + short-term block on batch-embeddings if throttling insufficient.
ryan-sre: agreed. I'll prepare the command. Mina, do you have the admin endpoint?
mina-eng: yup. Running locally. Command snippet: ```bash
# emergency per-org rate limit
curl -X POST https://admin.redwood.internal/api/v1/orgs/org_0x9a/rate-limits \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"scope":"org","limit_rpm":120,"reason":"emergency spike protection","actor":"oncall/sara"}'
```
sara-oncall: include a surge_window param so retries aren't instantly killed: surge_window=30s, enforcement_mode=soft.
mina-eng: updating payload and applying now.
mina-eng: POST returned 200. applied soft limit 120 rpm, surge_window=30s, enforcement=soft. audit id: audit_20270315_77.
incident-bot: Action recorded: org_rate_limit.update org_id=org_0x9a actor=sara-oncall audit=audit_20270315_77
sara-oncall: monitoring metrics now (p95, error rate, queue length).
ryan-sre: within 90s p95 dropped from 1.6s -> 0.85s, error rate down to 0.9%. queue depth normalized. good sign.
leo-support: customer acknowledged advisory: "we see backpressure, we'll stagger our rollout". no immediate ask to remove limits.
mina-eng: we still see a substream of heavy batch jobs hitting embeddings endpoint at 10x expected per-org concurrency. recommend additionally disabling batch-embeddings for that org for 10m window.
sara-oncall: do it if needed. prefer minimal user-visible impact. what's the admin command to disable a specific route?
mina-eng: ```bash
curl -X POST https://admin.redwood.internal/api/v1/orgs/org_0x9a/route-controls \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"route":"/v1/embeddings:batch","action":"disable","reason":"hotfix - spike"}'
```
mina-eng: applied route disable for /v1/embeddings:batch for org_0x9a. audit id audit_20270315_78.
ryan-sre: after disable, embeddings QPS for that org dropped 98%, overall p95 steady.
sara-oncall: good. leo/julie, please send a proactive note to the customer letting them know we applied temporary throttles and disabled batch embeddings to protect platform health and we can re-enable once they stagger. julie-cs to own comms.
julie-cs: sending a short note now. content: "We've applied temporary rate limits and paused batch-embeddings for your org to prevent service degradation. If you need immediate capacity, we can coordinate a short window to increase limits while we provision dedicated capacity."
leo-support: AM replied; they want the limit kept for now and will retry with lower concurrency.
ryan-sre: moving to post-incident steps: set a Canary rule to auto-shed for orgs exceeding 5x baseline w/in 60s. also add runbook link to the incident. Mina, can you make a quick PR to add the runbook pointer?
mina-eng: will open PR after stabilization.
sara-oncall: oncall handoff: I'm handing to ryan-sre for cleanup and postmortem. key facts: applied soft 120rpm limit + disabled batch endpoint. latency and error rate recovered. audit ids: 77,78. open action: add automated thresholds and CS follow-up. handoff at 08:15 UTC.
ryan-sre: acknowledged handoff. I'll keep watch for 30m, then kick postmortem.
incident-bot: Incident updates: severity=S2, start_ts=1779004321, mitigation=org_rate_limit + route_disable, lead=sara-oncall, status=stabilized
sara-oncall: small note for the postmortem: include graphs for per-org token distribution, autoscaler headroom, and customer rollout communication timeline.
ryan-sre: will draft. tagging @oncall-rotation for visibility.
mina-eng: follow-up item: add feature flag so we can rate-limit at endpoint-level per-org without disabling routes (less disruptive).
leo-support: kudos to team. :thumbsup:
sara-oncall: thanks everyone. closing thread once PM/CS signoff and postmortem scheduled.
ryan-sre: closing notes: rollback path is simply to DELETE the org rate-limit entry and re-enable route via admin endpoints (audit ids available).
incident-bot: Incident closed (stabilized -> monitoring) at 1779005889. Remember to file postmortem in /incidents/postmortems.
